size.notes: FishBase gives a 100 cm SL maximum and the Florida Museum 120 cm and 8 kg, but no fish that big is documented on hook and line. lengthCm.max set to 88 cm, where the Gulf of Mexico LWR meets the IGFA record.

spawn.notes: Spawns 65-80 km offshore over water deeper than 1,000 m; spawning temperature not given in the sources used.

migration.notes: Huge schools gather and head offshore in autumn and winter; juveniles return to estuaries at 16-20 mm (Florida Museum).

markings.where: upper half of the flank, lengthwise
markings.notes: several dark lines formed by a dark spot at the centre of each scale

pattern.fins: grey; two well-separated dorsal fins, the first spiny; short pectorals; 8 anal rays; body round in cross-section with a broad flat head and a fatty adipose eyelid over much of the eye

variants.juvenile: under 15 cm: plain silver with no stripes
variants.spawning_male: no distinct breeding colours described in the sources used

pattern.source: Florida Museum of Natural History striped mullet profile; FishBase diagnosis

regulations.notes: 50 striped and silver mullet per harvester in total; vessel limit 100 (Feb 1-Aug 31) or 50 (Sep 1-Jan 31); no size limit. Usually taken with a cast net. Simplified: the saltwater rule is applied in fresh water too.

economy.notes: A Gulf coast staple, sold fresh and smoked; the roe is prized. Fish from fresh water can taste muddy.

facts: Mullet swallow sand, which grinds their food in a muscular, gizzard-like stomach.
Adults tolerate everything from fresh water to 75 ppt, more than twice the salinity of the sea.
Sold as bait for billfish, a mullet is often worth more than it is as food.

research.task: Catch one on a pea of dough on a tiny hook
Photograph a mullet leaping clear of the water

ledger.wrenNote: Mullet don't want your lure, they want the scum on the grass. A pea of dough on a tiny hook, and watch the line, not the float. Soft mouth: easy does it.
